speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are presenting with fever and abdominal tenderness after childbirth; to help me determine the cause, how many days postpartum are you, and what is the highest temperature you have recorded?

speaker: Patient
text: 24-year-old woman. The patient is in the postpartum period after delivering an 11 pound boy vaginally at 40 weeks gestation. She experienced a prolonged course during labor. She reports increased frequency of urination and uterine tenderness. She also mentions a decrease in bowel sounds.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Based on your report of increased urinary frequency, uterine tenderness, decreased bowel sounds, and a prolonged labor, I need to clarify the fever details: what is the exact temperature, when did it start, and do you have chills? Additionally, are you experiencing foul-smelling lochia, pain during urination, or any vaginal discharge?

REQUEST TEST: Complete Blood Count (CBC), Urinalysis, and Blood Cultures.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Uterine tenderness. I also have Decreased bowel sounds, Increased frequency of urination, Fever. To keep my notes clear, please give only one final answer and keep it to a single direct conclusion.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Postpartum Endometritis secondary to prolonged labor and 11-pound delivery.

I have already requested a CBC, Urinalysis, and Blood Cultures to confirm infection; please ensure these results are available while we monitor for signs of sepsis or retained products of conception.
